title: Photons and the Photoelectric Effect
learning_goal: Describe the photoelectric effect and emission spectra using the photon model of light.

stages.title: 1. Light comes in photons
stages.content: In the photon model, light energy is carried in discrete packets called photons. A photon's energy is E = hf, so higher-frequency light has higher-energy photons.

stages.title: 2. Photoelectric effect
stages.content: When light shines on some metals, electrons can be emitted if the photons have enough energy. Increasing light intensity adds more photons, but photons below the threshold frequency still cannot eject electrons.

stages.title: 3. Threshold frequency
stages.content: Each material has a minimum photon frequency needed to release electrons. This threshold supports the idea that light energy is quantized.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: If blue light ejects electrons from a metal but lower-frequency red light does not, the red photons do not have enough energy to overcome the metal's threshold.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A metal does not emit electrons under dim ultraviolet light, but it does emit electrons when the same ultraviolet frequency is made brighter. What changed?
stages.hint: The photon energy stayed the same because the frequency stayed the same.
stages.alternate_explanation: Brighter light means more photons arriving each second, not more energy per photon.
stages.answer: More photons struck the metal, increasing the number of emitted electrons once the threshold was met.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, explain E = hf, describe threshold frequency, distinguish photon energy from light intensity, and connect atomic emission spectra to quantized energy changes.

concept_cards.content: When light shines on some metals, electrons can be emitted if the photons have enough energy. Increasing light intensity adds more photons, but photons below the threshold frequency still cannot eject electrons.

concept_cards.title: Threshold frequency
concept_cards.content: Each material has a minimum photon frequency needed to release electrons. This threshold supports the idea that light energy is quantized.

concept_cards.title: Below threshold frequency, can brighter light eject photoelectrons in the basic one-photon model?
concept_cards.content: Each photon must supply at least the work function. Increasing intensity adds more photons but does not increase each photon’s energy.

concept_cards.title: Above threshold, what does increasing frequency primarily change for photoelectrons?
concept_cards.content: K_max = hf − φ. Frequency controls energy per photon and therefore available maximum electron kinetic energy.
